newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-Lloyd not writing off NZ in one-dayers.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Lloyd not writing off NZ in one-dayers.

text.p: NAPIER, Feb 25 - England cricket coach David Lloyd isn't about to write off New Zealand in the one-day series, NZPA reported on Tuesday.
Even though England have done the hard work by taking a 2-0 lead in the five-game contest, Lloyd won't discount New Zealand's prospects of bouncing back.
Winning the last three matches, starting with the day-night match at McLean Park on Wednesday, will be a tall order for a New Zealand side out of sorts in recent games against England.
"We are playing a very good one-day team who are very proficient," Lloyd said yesterday.
"This is something they play a lot of. We do not play a lot of this style of cricket.
"But 2-0 up is a far better position than New Zealand are in. I'm delighted with the results, but I think we can improve."
Lloyd wants his players to learn during the one-day series here.

Although England have three domestic one-day competitions, they are relatively inexperienced playing international limited-overs rules, playing at night, with a white ball and two players in close catching positions for the first 15 overs.
"It's very new to the majority of our players," Lloyd said.
"The white ball is different, don't ask me why. With the lights, the razzmatazz, it's a terrific challenge, totally different for our lads and they're a bit open mouthed about it."

Lloyd said while winning the first two matches -- by four wickets at Lancaster Park last Thursday and by six wickets in a rain-reduced game in Auckland on Sunday -- had taken off some pressure, he wanted his players to press on and aim for a clean sweep.
And even though it was a week to go before the end of a long tour, there had been no talk among the players of mentally switching off and thinking of home.
"We've got three big matches to play, they're all important, there will be damn near full houses and there's a massive obligation to entertain.
"The one-day series is important coming at the end of the tour. We know we'll get judged on that.
"There're no thoughts that we've got to get back home, the place is beautiful and the people have been great."
England captain Mike Atherton missed the Auckland one-dayer with stiffness in his back.
It is a recurring problem for Atherton, and it's unlikely the England management will decide on whether he will play here until tomorrow morning.
England manager John Barclay wouldn't speculate on whether Atherton would have played at Auckland if it had been a test instead of a one-dayer.
However it is possible the tourists will again rest their skipper at Napier with the idea of having him fully fit for the last two matches of the tour.
For the New Zealand squad there will be no more chances if they lose at McLean Park.
Coach Steve Rixon predicted there would be changes after the second one-dayer if there wasn't a significant improvement.
However, the nature of Sunday's match -- where rain played a major part in the outcome and led to an artificial finish -- probably gave the players a stay of execution.
The same 12 players have been retained for Napier, but another loss seems sure to bring changes for the last two one-dayers.

Canterbury left armer Geoff Allott should get a game here, after being 12th man for the first two matches, probably at the expense of either Heath Davis or Simon Doull, neither of whom impressed at Auckland.
Adam Parore is the batsman most at risk after making 26 off 52 balls at Christchurch and being run out, backing up too far, for two last Sunday.
The umpires are Chris King of Queenstown and David Quested of Christchurch, with Evan Watkin of Wellington the third official.

New Zealand: Lee Germon (captain), Bryan Young, Nathan Astle, Adam Parore, Stephen Fleming, Chris Cairns, Chris Harris, Dipak Patel, Gavin Larsen, Simon Doull, Heath Davis, Geoff Allott (one to be omitted).

England: Mike Atherton (captain), Nick Knight, Alec Stewart, Nasser Hussain, Graham Thorpe, John Crawley, Ronnie Irani, Craig White, Dominic Cork, Robert Croft, Darren Gough, Andrew Caddick, Chris Silverwood, Alan Mullally, Phil Tufnell (four to be omitted).
